title: KorWF-Pi configuration
description: All user-facing policy for KorWF-Pi (PLAN §3.J). Every field has a default; an empty object `{}` is a valid, working, no-Jev configuration. Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express are listed in docs/config-reference.md §Validation rules and enforced by src/config validation.

configVersion.description: Schema version of this file. Bumped on breaking changes; the loader migrates or refuses.

ModelRef.description: Fully qualified `<provider>/<modelId>` as shown by Pi's model registry.

NonNegativeOrNull.description: `null` means no cap of this kind.

allowlist.description: Optional filter over the models Pi already has configured (PLAN §3.D). Empty lists mean 'all configured'. The system never uses a provider or model outside this list.

providers.description: Provider ids eligible for selection. `[]` = every provider Pi has configured.

models.description: Fully qualified model refs eligible for selection. `[]` = every model of an eligible provider.

pins.description: Task kind → model ref. A pinned model is never overridden by fallback without asking (PLAN §3.D).

routeMainSession.description: Opt-in: allow KorWF to switch the main Pi session's own model at safe boundaries (PLAN §3.D 'Main session'). Default off; the user's own session is never re-routed without opting in.

overrides.description: Per-model card overrides (PLAN §3.D layer 3). Keys are model refs.

TaskKind.description: Task kinds used for pins and fallback policy. `default` applies where no specific kind is set.

BudgetCaps.description: Matches the `Budget` record in docs/records.md. `null` = no cap of this kind. All numeric caps are >= 0.

Budgets.description: Hard-stop caps (PLAN §2.6). Exceeding any cap stops the scope and surfaces a resumable state. Task <= phase <= workflow is enforced by the validator when both are non-null.

jev.description: Per-workflow cap on Jev (TypeSafe) spend, separate from model spend. Irrelevant when Jev is disabled.

costEstimateBeforeRun.description: Show a cost estimate and require confirmation before `run` begins (PLAN §2.6).

Mode.description: Operating mode (docs/records.md `WorkflowMode`). Shadow: observe and record only, no mutation. Advisory: propose, never act. Supervised: act only on explicit approval. Bounded autonomous: act within budgets and approval classes.

ApprovalDecision.description: PLAN §2.6: auto = pre-approved for the mode; queue = block this task, continue others, notify; stop = stop the phase and wait for the user.

HighRiskPolicy.description: High-risk classes (PLAN §7) are `stop` in every mode; the schema forbids any other value so config cannot weaken it.

NoAutoPolicy.description: Classes that may be `queue` or `stop` but never `auto` in any mode (PLAN §3.C: no silent scope expansion). Not PLAN §7 high-risk, so `queue` is allowed.

queueTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a queued approval waits before the task is marked blocked. 0 = wait indefinitely (never auto-approve on timeout).

classes.description: Action class → decision per mode (docs/approval-classes.md, src/workflow/approval-classes.ts). Configurable classes accept any decision (validator V4 still forbids `auto` for mutation classes in shadow/advisory); `scope_change`/`replan` are never `auto`; high-risk classes (PLAN §7) are fixed to `stop`.

ShippedDenyPaths.description: Shipped minimum deny list of path globs (PLAN §7). `privacy.denyPaths` MUST contain every entry; the `allOf`/`contains` constraints below enforce it in-schema.

ShippedDenyPatterns.description: Shipped minimum deny list of content regexes (ECMAScript syntax, compiled with flags `iu`, applied per line). `privacy.denyPatterns` MUST contain every entry.

Privacy.description: Data policy (PLAN §7). Default-deny outbound for secrets and sensitive paths; minimal snippets; raw logging opt-in.

denyPaths.description: Path globs never read into outbound context or logs. Must be a superset of `$defs/ShippedDenyPaths`; entries can be added, never removed.

denyPatterns.description: Content regexes; a matching line is redacted before any outbound request or log write. Must be a superset of `$defs/ShippedDenyPatterns`.

allowPaths.description: Explicit per-project carve-outs (e.g. `docs/fixtures/.env.example`). A carve-out must not be broader than the deny entry it relaxes; validator rule V7.

maxSnippetBytes.description: Largest single file excerpt sent to Jev or a model provider.

maxRequestBytes.description: Hard cap on outbound request body size (256 KiB).

sendFilePaths.description: Send project-relative paths with snippets. Absolute paths are never sent.

sendRepoIdentity.description: Include remote URL / repo name in Jev context. Off: only a hash.

rawLogging.description: Opt-in raw request/response payload logging (PLAN §7). Off by default.

redactBeforeWrite.description: Deny patterns are applied before writing raw logs. Fixed true.

firstUseDisclosure.description: Show which data classes go to TypeSafe and to model providers before the first outbound request.

MidTaskPolicy.description: On a cap mid-task: hand off with an explicit handoff packet and intact worktree, or restart the task (PLAN §3.D).

Fallback.description: Caps and fallback (PLAN §3.D). Applies when a model is capped (quota, rate limit, budget) or unavailable.

midTaskPolicy.description: Task kind → mid-task policy. `default` is required and covers unlisted kinds.

dwell.description: Anti-oscillation: minimum time on the fallback model before the primary is retried.

preferWaitIfResetWithinMinutes.description: If the primary cap is estimated to clear within N minutes, wait instead of switching to a more expensive substitute. 0 = never wait.

retryPrimaryAtTaskBoundary.description: Retry the primary at the next task boundary once the cap is estimated cleared; never re-probe every task. Fixed true.

staticOrder.description: Ordered model refs used when Jev is unavailable or answers none/unknown. Must be a subset of the effective allowlist (validator rule V1). `[]` = Pi registry order filtered by allowlist.

allCappedBehaviour.description: All candidates capped → pause the phase, surface state, resume when a cap clears. Not a failure. Fixed.

overridePins.description: Pinned models are never overridden by fallback without asking. Fixed false.

Jev.description: TypeSafe/Jev transport (docs/adr/0003-jev-transport.md). With no key the product runs in optional mode: deterministic workflow only.

enabled.description: Master switch. Off by default; with no key it is treated as off even when true.

baseUrl.description: API origin. HTTPS only. Configurable for users who proxy.

keySource.description: How the API key is resolved. Never the key itself.

name.description: Env var name (kind=env) or secret name (kind=pi_secrets).

Notifications.description: Notification hooks (PLAN §2.6). Only the in-Pi channel is on by default; nothing leaves the machine unless configured.

ui.description: Pi UI notify/status (no-op when `ctx.hasUI` is false).

desktop.description: OS desktop notification via the platform notifier, if present.

command.description: Run a user-supplied executable with a JSON event on stdin. Off by default; counts as `run_shell` for approvals.

webhook.description: POST the event JSON to an HTTPS URL. Off by default; payload is redacted with deny patterns.

Storage.description: On-disk state (src/storage/paths.ts). Namespaced under the project; never in the source tree outside this directory.

path.description: Override for the storage root. Relative to the project root; absolute allowed only with `allowOutsideProject`. `null` = `<project>/.korwf`.

allowOutsideProject.description: Permit an absolute `path` outside the project root.

Recovery.description: Bounded recovery policy (PLAN §3.G). Every response is drawn from a fixed menu and every count is capped; the last response is always `ask_user` or `stop`.

maxAttemptsPerTask.description: Hard ceiling on attempts for one task, counting the first. Reaching it ends recovery with `ask_user` or `stop`; nothing may raise it mid-task.

maxAttemptsPerPhase.description: Hard ceiling on recovery rounds for one phase gate.

maxEvidenceGatherings.description: How often `gather_evidence` may be chosen for one subject before it stops being an option. Gathering evidence forever is a stall, not a recovery.

maxReplans.description: How often `replan` may be chosen for one subject.

maxModelFallbacks.description: How often `fallback_model` may be chosen for one subject. The route itself is chosen by `fallback` (PLAN §3.D), not here.

maxWorkerChanges.description: How often `change_worker` may be chosen for one subject.

requireReconciliationBeforeRetry.description: A step that may have had side effects is never retried until its outcome is reconciled. Fixed true: PLAN §3.G, and a config that could switch it off would be a way to permit a double effect.

unreconcilableSideEffect.description: Response when a side-effecting step cannot be reconciled (no probe, or the probe itself failed). Never `retry`.

finalResponse.description: Response once the ladder is exhausted. Both options are terminal; unattended runs that must not queue a question set `stop`.

Verification.description: Evidence-gap evaluators (PLAN §2.4 (2), §3.F; issue #47). Condition 2 of the task gate. Defaults are conservative and an override may only make a threshold stricter — a config that tries to lower a floor is ignored on that field, so a bad value can never open the gate. With Jev disabled the mapping rule still applies: every acceptance criterion needs at least one linked passing check and one passing evidence item.

thresholds.description: Per-risk-class threshold overrides. Omitted classes use the shipped defaults in `src/verification/evaluate.ts`.

low.description: Thresholds for one risk class. Every value is a floor or a ceiling; `src/verification/evaluate.ts` may only tighten them, never loosen them.

claimConfidence.description: Minimum confidence for a `supported` completion-claim answer to count. Below it the answer is an abstention, and an abstention is a gap.

gapCeiling.description: Highest probability-of-gap that still counts as `no gap`. A noul near the middle is not evidence of absence.

testExercisesMinLevel.description: Lowest `verify.test_exercises@1` level that credits a test as exercising the criterion.

requireExercisingTest.description: Whether a criterion whose linked tests are all below the level floor is a gap on its own.

medium.description: Thresholds for one risk class. Every value is a floor or a ceiling; `src/verification/evaluate.ts` may only tighten them, never loosen them.

claimConfidence.description: Minimum confidence for a `supported` completion-claim answer to count. Below it the answer is an abstention, and an abstention is a gap.

gapCeiling.description: Highest probability-of-gap that still counts as `no gap`. A noul near the middle is not evidence of absence.

testExercisesMinLevel.description: Lowest `verify.test_exercises@1` level that credits a test as exercising the criterion.

requireExercisingTest.description: Whether a criterion whose linked tests are all below the level floor is a gap on its own.

high.description: Thresholds for one risk class. Every value is a floor or a ceiling; `src/verification/evaluate.ts` may only tighten them, never loosen them.

claimConfidence.description: Minimum confidence for a `supported` completion-claim answer to count. Below it the answer is an abstention, and an abstention is a gap.

gapCeiling.description: Highest probability-of-gap that still counts as `no gap`. A noul near the middle is not evidence of absence.

testExercisesMinLevel.description: Lowest `verify.test_exercises@1` level that credits a test as exercising the criterion.

requireExercisingTest.description: Whether a criterion whose linked tests are all below the level floor is a gap on its own.

maxExcerptBytes.description: Largest test-file or evidence excerpt put into a question state. `privacy.outbound` caps again afterwards; this is the evaluator's own ceiling so the full diff is never the input.

ReviewPolicy.description: Independent review contexts (PLAN §2.4 (3), §3.F; issue #48). Which changes require an independent coding-model review in a fresh context that never sees the worker's claim. A review is evidence for gate condition 3, never authority: it cannot set `done`, and an unresolved blocking finding refuses the gate until a recheck at a newer revision passes. High-risk tasks always require review whatever these rules say.

reviewEverything.description: Require an independent review for every change. Turning this on only tightens the policy; turning it off never removes a rule, and high-risk tasks are reviewed regardless.

rules.description: Additional rules, each naming change classes and/or ownership path prefixes that require review from a minimum risk class upwards. These are added to the shipped defaults in `src/verification/review.ts`; a rule can only make review required, never optional.

id.description: Stable rule id, reported as the reason review was required.

changeClasses.description: Change classes this rule fires for, as classified by `src/git/`. Empty means any class.

paths.description: Repository-relative path prefixes. Empty means any path.

minRiskClass.description: Lowest task risk class at which this rule fires.

preferDifferentModelFamily.description: Prefer a reviewer from a different model family than the one that produced the work (.pi/skills/jev-orchestration/SKILL.md §4). A same-family review is still recorded, with a caveat on its evidence row, so a single-family configuration can still review.
